title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 46
paragraphs: In the next year after this, Darius first sent a messenger to the men of Thasos, who had been accused by their neighbors of planning revolt, and ordered them to take down the wall around their town and bring their ships to Abdera. The Thasians in fact, having been besieged by Histiaeus the Milesian and at the same time having large revenues coming in, had been using their money to build warships and to surround their city with a stronger wall. Now the revenues came to them from the mainland and from the mines: from the gold mines in Scapte Hyle there came in usually eighty talents a year, and from those on Thasos itself a smaller amount than this—but so much that, in general, the Thasians, without any tax on the produce of their soil, had a revenue from the mainland and from the mines amounting yearly to two hundred talents, and when the amount was at its highest, to three hundred.
